summary.headline: Moneyboxx Q1 FY27 disbursements fell to INR77 crore from INR92 crore as AUM reached INR832 crore; management guides to normalised disbursements by January 2027.
summary.overview: Q1 FY27 was a transition quarter in which Moneyboxx deliberately shifted toward secured, higher-ticket and higher-bureau-score loans, which cut disbursements and income. Disbursements were INR77 crore versus INR92 crore a year earlier, and total income was INR52.12 crore. Net interest and fee income fell to INR31.02 crore from INR38.52 crore, NIM dropped to 12.3% from 14.36%, and PAT was INR0.21 crore versus INR0.24 crore. Management pointed to partnership channels, solar lending and a digital product as the next growth drivers, with secured AUM targeted at about 80% by March 2027.

segments.name: Secured lending
segments.commentary: Secured loans were 87% of Q1 disbursements vs 67% in FY26; secured book is about 75% of AUM (incl. DLFG-backed loans) vs 49% in June 2025. Target is about 80% by March 2027.

segments.name: Unsecured lending
segments.commentary: Unsecured lending now about 13% of lending, down from 100% at start. Stopped from April 2026 except via partnership model and in Punjab.

segments.name: Renewable energy (solar) loans
segments.commentary: Cumulative disbursements crossed INR10 crore by July 2026; monthly disbursement grew from INR0.3 crore (first month) to INR5 crore (latest), with INR7 crore targeted for August and about INR20 crore per month by January. Target about 10% of AUM by end FY27; 15% of July disbursements.

segments.name: Partnership channel
segments.commentary: Partnerships were 15% of July disbursements, targeted at 20% in September-October and at least 30% by January 2027. Solar yield is about 23%; dairy partnership yield targeted at about 22%; opex expected at 1-1.5%.

guidance_outlook: Disbursements expected to normalise by Q4 FY27 (around January 2027), per management, with the pace 'maybe even sometimes better than peers'.
Secured share of AUM targeted at about 80% by March 2027, including guarantee-backed loans.
Renewable energy loans targeted at about 10% of AUM by end FY27, implying roughly INR80-85 crore of AUM per the analyst's framing.
AUM of INR1,600-1,700 crore cited as the level at which profitability 'will completely change', with opex held at current levels.
Partnership share of monthly business targeted at 20% in Sept-Oct and at least 30% by January 2027.
Institutional equity infusion expected in H2 FY27; company said it aims to raise equity from institutions this year.
capex_capacity: Branch consolidation done in the quarter; closed some rural branches. Per-branch savings of about INR1-1.25 lakh per month (fixed staff and rent); quantified annual savings not given.
Moneyboxx One loan origination system launched May 2026 and now live; Sikka app, Cattle AI and MBCollect platforms also in use.
Headcount described as flat to slightly declining; solar disbursement of INR5 crore run by five people with no dedicated sales or collection team.
Dairy partnership expected to start disbursing from the month after the call (about September 2026) at INR3-5 crore per month.
demand_pricing: Disbursements moderated as the company stopped unsecured lending from April 2026 (except partnerships and Punjab) and stopped secured loans below INR5 lakh (except some solar branches). About 70% of disbursements were above INR5 lakh and about 75% went to customers with bureau score of 650 and above.
Management attributed the lag versus peers to team transition, the time needed to retrain staff for property-backed sourcing, and earlier higher cost of lending.

Partnership yields are said to be lower in headline terms, offset by lower acquisition cost and default loss guarantee (FLDG) protection. Solar credit cost expected to be under 0.5% for FY27; competitors cited at 3-5% without guarantees.
Management said the company is targeting INR8-15 lakh tickets as the core segment, which it views as offering lower credit cost and reasonable yields.

qa_highlights.question: Why are peers growing AUM and disbursements faster, and is it secured-mix transition, sourcing or branch productivity?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited the April 2026 stop on unsecured lending in MP, Chhattisgarh, Haryana and Rajasthan, the move to larger tickets, and team retraining. It said it expects normalised disbursements by January 2027.

qa_highlights.question: Is the unsecured lending stop permanent?
qa_highlights.answer: Not fully. Unsecured lending will continue under guarantee-backed partnerships such as a dairy tie-up with FLDG, and digital small-ticket unsecured loans with higher yields are planned.

qa_highlights.question: What is the partnership contribution and its economics?
qa_highlights.answer: Partnerships were 15% of July disbursements, targeted at 20% in Sept-Oct and 30% by January. Solar yields about 23%, dairy about 22%, opex 1-1.5%, with FLDG and sometimes incentive programmes.

qa_highlights.question: What happens to credit quality when FLDG guarantees are removed?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said solar loans are asset-backed with 20% customer contribution and payments go directly to OEM/EPC, so guarantees should be durable. It estimated INR300-500 crore of guarantee programmes are obtainable; if guarantees end, yields would be revisited.

qa_highlights.question: Operating leverage and branch savings?
qa_highlights.answer: Opex is flat in absolute terms, and the company says the key is AUM growth; the spread of 12-13% covers opex. Branch closures save about INR1-1.25 lakh per branch per month. A quantified total saving was not given.

qa_highlights.question: Debt and equity requirements for the FY27 plan?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said about INR80 crore of monthly debt is needed to cover repayments of INR30-40 crore a month. INR70 crore of NCDs was raised in April-July, including INR50 crore from Capri Global, and a INR100 crore term sheet from a global impact fund is in hand. Equity is expected from institutions this year.

risks_watch: Disbursement recovery hinges on a January 2027 normalisation; management said it is 'not one or two months' away, so Q2 FY27 disbursements are the first checkpoint.
Partnership ramp: share of monthly business must rise from 15% (July) to 20% in Sept-Oct and at least 30% by January 2027; the first partnership took 6-8 months to build.

Credit quality of guarantee-backed book: yields and credit cost depend on FLDG and guarantee programmes; management estimated INR300-500 crore of guarantees is obtainable, and said yields would be revisited if guarantees end.
Opex of INR28.59 crore is flat, so profitability depends on AUM growth to the INR1,600-1,700 crore range; AUM was INR832 crore in June 2026.
Funding: about INR80 crore a month of debt is needed against INR30-40 crore monthly repayments; institutional equity is targeted in H2 FY27 but not yet secured.
Margin trend: NIM fell to 12.3% from 14.36%, and PAT was INR0.21 crore; watch whether the borrowing cost decline of 12.5% materialises.
key_quotes: Q1 FY27 was an important transition quarter for us.
I think by January, the fourth quarter of this year should see very normalized disbursements.
So even if I have say, 5% going in the worst case, which is not likely now because there is -- we are seeing a significant support from dealers also in these collections.
Yes, we need to significantly grow our AUM at this stage.
summary.management_tone: Management was confident on the strategic direction and the January 2027 normalisation, but cautious and vague on near-term numbers: it did not quantify branch cost savings, gave no equity timeline beyond H2 FY27, and acknowledged that AUM growth and disbursements lag peers.

adds.what: Dairy partnership disbursing INR3-5 crore per month (new lending channel, not physical capacity)
Solar renewable energy loan book targeted at ~10% of AUM by end FY27 (about INR80-85 crore per analyst framing)

growth.why: Disbursements fell to INR77 crore from INR92 crore YoY and PAT slipped to INR0.21 crore from INR0.24 crore, with NIM down to 12.3% from 14.36%; management promises normalisation by January 2027 and new solar/partnership channels, but no revenue growth figure is guided and the AUM growth is only 5% underlying, so the outlook is flat.
